Model Text Summary:
A satirical poem by Reginald Arkell exploring situational irony and subjective enthusiasm. The speaker visits Mrs. Jones, who boasts about her grand 'rock garden'. Instead of scenic natural rock formations, the speaker discovers a patch filled literally with broken concrete slabs and urban debris. The poem plays on the double meaning of 'concrete' and pokes lighthearted fun at human exaggeration.
